notes.title: The Origins of Wax Heads
notes.notes:
[p]Hey Wax Heads,[/p][p]We've got something a little bit different today. We wanted to cover the origins of Wax Heads, our inspirations and a bunch of behind the scenes, If you want to know a little bit more about us and the making of the game, read on...[b]

What was the first spark that led to the idea of Wax Heads?[/b][/p][p][b]Murray:[/b] I’ve pretty much always been a big music fan (shock, horror). I grew up on a diet of Pink Floyd and Queen growing up, but from the age of 12 and buying my first album (Eminem - Marshall Mathers LP) I’ve had the music bug.

I would watch MTV2 and Kerrang TV and devour music videos and read all the ravings of my favourite bands when I was a teen, and as soon as I was able, I then  started going to gigs, and then even playing in bands myself.

It’s probably no surprise that with this long interest, that it might one day overlap with my parallel passion for Video Games.  I had long thought about how there weren't really a lot of games about music culturally. I mean there were games mechanically about music, in which you would do the act of performing music (i.e guitar hero), but there were very few games that explored why we love music and what music means to us.

[i](Disclaimer: There are more games in recent memory that have explored this, but at the original inception of Wax Heads it was a smaller pool.)

[/i]One of the first times I saw something actually capture that feeling was playing ‘Night In the Woods’ during the band mini game. The endearing appeal of getting to live in the skin of four friends playing in a band in their little town really resonated with me. I wanted to experience a game solely about that experience.

Before working on Wax Heads I actually had my first whack at making a game about music when working at Triple Topping, a Danish Game studio, where I pitched “Dead Pets Unleashed”, a game about being a demonic punk band trying to navigate the building pressures of adulthood and being in a band as you turn 30. I unfortunately didn’t get to see the game finish as I moved back to the UK to be closer to family for my kids.

So I felt like I had unfinished business with trying to articulate my love of music in games. I just didn’t know exactly how, especially already trying the “I used to be in a band route”. Whatever I did next had to be something that felt different from Dead Pets, but still allowed me to express my love for music.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Did the concept emerge during a game jam or during a more organic moment of inspiration?[/b][/p][p][b]Murray: [/b]The exact eureka moment for Wax Heads came when playing “Wilmot’s Warehouse”.  It’s no secret that I love vinyl records, I’ve been collecting them since my mid 20s and so when I was playing Wilmot and looking at all these jazzy, little graphic tiles, I thought to myself “wouldn’t it be so cool if this was actually a record store and I was organising all different records / finding them to give to customers.

That was what sparked the idea of “game in a record store” - I just wasn’t sure how it would work mechanically. The first thought was to try and explore something procedurally generating and modular, but then I remembered I don’t have the brain to design that.

Instead I followed my love for Papers Please, and was inspired by the likes of Strange Horticulture / Coffee Talk / VA11 HA11 A to make a game that takes place in a record shop front, with logical deduction puzzles to figure out records to give out. (You know but it also includes fun writing and visually interesting characters).

I mocked up the first iteration of Wax Heads in Twine on my own as a [url="https://murraysomerwolff.itch.io/wax-heads-prototype"][u]proof of concept[/u][/url], with my thinking being that if my janky web text game is fun, then surely a more sophisticated version would be a lot more.

Luckily the proof of concept seemed to work, and even more luckily was strong enough for me to convince Rothio to take a punt and try working with me to make Wax Heads a reality, using her technical wizardry to lift my cobbled together word adventure into a living, breathing world.

Immediately from seeing Wax Heads playing in Godot, in an actual gaming interface, powered by Rothio’s coding magic, that was when we knew this game had real promise.

[b]Rothio: [/b]When Murray came to me with the first concept of Wax Heads, which at that time was just some illustrations and an interactive dialogue to go with them, in my head I could already see how adding interactivity, movement, and life to each character and story was something I really wanted to do. I’ve been lucky to be part of this and help it grow into the universe it is today.[/p][p][/p][p][b]How did the title Wax Heads come about and were there earlier title names?[/b] [/p][p][b]Murray: [/b]There’s a bit of secret lore here, but a lot of the names of projects come from my wife, Daisy. She coined the name “Wax Heads” early on, it was meant only as a placeholder but it sounded punchy and accurate, without appearing derivative and nothing else has come close to replacing it. So Wax Heads just stuck.

Daisy also named our game studio, “Patattie Games” (combining Spanish patatas and Scottish tatties together). So she’s our unofficial-official-naming exec.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Was there something about this kind of game that you want people to experience? Any shared appreciations?[/b] [/p][p]With wanting to make Wax Heads, we wanted to create a game that really captures the endearing love of creativity. The way it makes you swell up inside when you hear a new song you fall in love with for the first time, or you discover a new band / artist / TV Show which is your current favourite and you just feel the need to tell someone about it.

Especially in an age where every day brings a new fresh discourse about AI and how impersonal and bland everything has become, we wanted to celebrate the beauty of all things music, something which is such a big part of the human experience, and is all around us.

We want people to find that everywhere in Wax Heads, in the plethora of visual art drawn, in the too-good-to-be-true soundtrack music, in the imagination of the bands and records, in the writing and care put into every character. We’ve crammed so much of our own genuine, unadulterated love for music, art, story and games that we want that sincerity to reach out through the game and hopefully encourage players to connect with their own relationship with creativity.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Were there any creative influences behind the game?[/b][/p][p][b]Murray: [/b]There’s quite an extensive list of influences that drive behind this game for me personally, so I’ll dish out some of the top picks in different categories:

[b]Books: [/b][i]Please Kill Me / Kim Gordon: Girl in a band / Kathleen Hanna: Rebel Girl / Our Band Could Be Your Life

[/i][b]Film: [/b][i]Dig! (documentary) / Meet Me in The Bathroom (documentary) / The Punk Singer (Documentary) / High Fidelity / Daria (series) / American Movie

[/i][b]Visual:[/b] Scott Pilgrim, both from the comics and the recent animated series, has been a particularly strong influence, as a visual style and also a quality to which we’ve compared ourselves to throughout.

Lastly, the band The Replacements, they mean a lot to me and have this kind of underdog, plucky, world on your shoulders/against you vibe, they just remain a guiding light to this project.[/p][p][/p][p][b]How did you get to where you are now? Were there any "A-ha!" moments?[/b][/p][p][b]Murray: [/b]The biggest “A-ha” moment for me when making Wax Heads was when we iterated on the navigation of exploring the store when looking for a record.

Originally the plan was to have just two different record shelves you swapped between, devoid of any real sense of place. But instead we created a movement system that means you actually move between rooms in the store, giving spaces character, allowing more opportunity for personality and detail, the store becomes intimately known.

As soon as we implemented it in the game, I could feel Repeater Records actually coming to life and it being somewhere I wanted to spend time in.

[b]Rothio: [/b]I think the most important moment I remember was when I designed all the interaction for the controller. The game was already set up to work with the mouse, but we had to redesign all the controls so navigating the UI with the controller was possible, which is really complex and has many layers of interfaces stacked on top of each other. As someone who hates virtual cursors when playing with a controller, I wanted to create a ui navigation flow specifically for the controller. The cool thing is that not only did we manage to create really solid controller support and adapt all the functionality we already had, but it also improved the layout of the different elements we had designed for the mouse. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Is there something you've always wanted where only Wax Heads really scratches that itch?[/b][/p][p][b]Murray: [/b]A perfect excuse for me to nerd out about music as much as I want but for it to be actually substantial to the project and world I’m building. Nothing else can scratch that itch, trust me I’ve tried!

[b]Rothio: [/b]Making a game that anyone can play, so even people who aren’t used to playing and just want to enjoy the game at their own pace can do it, while those who are more used to this kind of format still find it interesting. It’s the same with the music. Murray has made a game that people who are really into music will enjoy because of all the references and details, but people who aren’t that deep into it can still enjoy the characters, the stories, and the culture that comes through the music.[/p][p]I think we’ve created the perfect experience for that, and I can’t imagine a better game for it.[/p][p][/p][p]Take care and keep on spinning 💿[/p][p][i]Murray & Rothio <3[/i][/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Top picks for Glastonbury 2025!
notes.notes: [p]Hey fellow Wax Heads collectors,[/p][p]We are sure you are aware that one of the best music festivals opened its gates today, Glastonbury festival at Worthy Farm in the UK!  Abi, Paul and Tee from Repeater Records have selected their top three acts to share with you so if you are lucky enough to be there, consider checking them out![/p][p][/p][p]Up first, Abi:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44982268/e4dbf8056004137b015ccb8ea1e8a7eb6643e82a.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Amyl and the Sniffers:[/b] "Have you seen the charisma that oozes from Amy Taylor? They're so damn cool and their songs rock so hard. They're like if Bad Toes and Sister made a band together",[/p][p][b]Japanese Breakfast[/b]: "I love, love, love a good indie rock hook and Michelle Zauner seems to effortlessly conjure them. The song "Everybody wants to love you" is one of my faves. So addictive, Girl Junk are inspired by those melodies, although the vocal style is more like Leah Weber?",[/p][p][b]TV on the radio[/b]: "I've wanted to see these guys for like FOREVER - got so much ,spit spirit and soul in their songs, you can't help but rock out to it. They're like a groovier version of Brick Dog, have all the power but with an infectious rhythm underneath".[/p][p][/p][p]Paul:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44982268/68e96bba6da6b167195d7a0bb939b1e0a05657df.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Charlie XCX[/b]: "Oh my god girl, Charlie is the girl of the MOMENT, you cannot miss the chance to see her, she's as hot a ticket as Mimi, so you know you're in for an unforgettable time with that star power",[/p][p][b]Alanis Morissette[/b]:"Enjoying an absolute iconic diva do her thing? That wouldn't be ironic in my book, cause enjoying prestige queens like this is a guilt free joy! Makes me think of the time I saw 90s Spanish icon Maria Estrella, and that was one of THE.BEST.NIGHTS.OF.MY.LIFE, so yes girl let's go, because everything is gonna be fine, fine, FINE!",[/p][p][b]Scissor Sisters[/b]: "Unabashed queer electro pop that's deliriously camp and fun? Um, yes please! Have you heard the song Invisible Light? I revisit that music video at least once every 6 months. You don't get bands like Gecko Jester and Pink Sq. without the likes of Scissor Sisters, so sign me up, I will see you in the crowd honey!.[/p][p][/p][p]Tee:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44982268/76293373bf463fd403faca3481053ba3b1d08524.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Four Tet & Floating Points[/b]: "Look. Festivals aren't my thing and I don't love big ques and crowds... BUT if you're gonna bring the likes of electro powerhouses Four Tet and Floating Points to your line up, I begrudgingly choose to attend cause you just know they're gonna transport you out of that mud entrenched hellscape to a serotonin powered highway of stomach knotting drops and hooks. And they're like the best of the best, sitting up there alongside Roberta D and Shy Robot."[/p][p][b]Denzel Curry[/b]: "AND if I was already gonna be forced to attend, I would totally check out Denzel Curry, his rap is layered and packed full of punching rhymes, I love his range and I've heard live that it's a real live wire act, so it sounds worth checking out. I saw RXX and Nia Pixel do a double headlining show recently and that was actually really fun, so I think I'd be in for a similar good time. IF I was going that is (Which I'm not...)[/p][p][/p][p]Enjoy the festival - there or watching from home![/p]

notes.title: Wax Heads livestream Sunday at 12:00 PDT / 20:00 BST on Cerebral Puzzle Showcase
notes.notes:
Hello Repeater Record custodians,

We are excited to announce that Wax Heads has been invited back again to the Cerebral Puzzle Showcase which is coming to Steam this weekend!  

Murray and Rothio from Patattie Games will be livestreaming the Wax Heads demo plus the first chapter  on Sunday night at 12:00 PDT / 15:00 EDT / 20:00 BST/ 21:00 CET!

It’s been a year since they last showed their initial demo at Cerebral Puzzle Showcase and they’re so excited to catch up on what development has been like since. Chatting about their favourite new features, unexpected obstacles and how it feels for the game to have recently reached Alpha.   

Come and hang out, listen to them laugh at some of their craziest ideas (some of which might make it into the game with enough peer pressure) and even ask questions of your own! 

Cerebral Puzzle Showcase is organised by Draknek & Friends, an award-winning developer and publisher of lovingly crafted puzzle games. For over a decade, they've been crafting high quality, rewarding, and elegant puzzle experiences that take a theme, mechanic, or ludicrous idea and push it to its natural conclusion.

Wax Heads Streaming Sunday 1st June at at 12:00 PDT / 15:00 EDT / 20:00 BST/ 21:00 CET

Take care and keep spinning,

Murray and Rothio

notes.title: Record Store Day
notes.notes:
Hello fellow Wax Head collectors,

Ahead of Record Store Day this Saturday 12th April we took a look at the list to pick out what we would be buying at our local record store, and what a selection it is!  After a lot of thought and deliberation we whittled it down to our top 5:

[b]No. 1 - Flying Lotus ‘Spirit Box’[/b]

I’ve been a huge fan of Flying Lotus for years, love his albums (‘Until the Quiet Comes’ is my personal fav record, but ‘Parisian Goldfish’ is my favourite song). He also does incredible live shows (he remixes of Ghost in the Shell and FF7 Shinra Theme) Needless to say, whenever he puts out new music, it’s an instant must get for me.

[b]No. 2 - Slint - ‘Tweez (Tweethan Mix)[/b]

Slint’s ‘Spiderland’ is up there as an all timer cherished album, but maybe, quite unfairly, I’ve never really given its predecessor ‘Tweez’ a proper chance. That’s what I love about record store day, it’s an excuse to indulge in records I might not otherwise do. 

[b]No. 3 - Rival Consoles - ‘Howl’[/b]

Wax Heads is known for its post-punk aesthetic and sensibilities, but what people may not know is it also carries my deep love for electronic music. ‘Howl’ by Rival Consoles is an awesome listen and since I actually don’t own it yet on vinyl, it might be time to rectify that for Record Store Day.

[b]No. 4 - Throwing Muses - ‘Live in Providence, 1992’[/b]

Throwing Muses are a band I’ve gotten into recently and they exude this effortlessly cool, melancholic sunshine vibe that really describes what Repeater Records is all about in Wax Heads. A band as seasoned as this, you know a Live album is gonna be great. 

[b]No. 5 - The Replacements - ‘Tim’[/b]

Okay so look this one is cheating - I already own this Ed Stadium remixed deluxe edition of The Replacement’s seminal album ‘Tim’. But it’s so good I would honestly just buy it all over again. Not only is this album EXCELLENT with hit after hit (Bastards of young, Left of the dial, Swinging Party etc.) and have a great closing track which is featured in the awesome cartoon Regular Show (Here Comes a Regular) - BUT The Replacements are to me (Murray) the spirit album of what Wax Heads is all about. Their inscrutable, underdog music is what being in a band and loving music is all about, warts and all. So yes, this album rocks and it belongs very much in your collection.

Let us know what you would pick up from the list? - https://www.recordstoreday.co.uk/rsd-list


Take care and keep on spinning -

Murray & Rothio

notes.title: Oh my God... Wax Heads Demo Now Has Full Controller Support!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44982268/04167c8e848e481ac3e75254b27261854abc9d31.png[/img]

Good afternoon Repeater Record custodians - just a quick post from us!

Wax Heads is part of Wholesome Games Steam Event, and so to celebrate we've updated the demo with some small QoL updates aaaaand... [b] FULL CONTROLLER SUPPORT!!! [/b]

Which means you can now sit back, cozy up with a controller and play the demo at whatever your preferred comfort position. It's something Rothio has been working on and I have to say we're both very happy and think it's already feeling reaaally good! 

[i](it's even now our preferred way of playing the game)[/i]

But please do let us know what you think, your constructive feedback is very welcome.

Beyond that, we still have our broadcast of the dev chat between myself & Rothio and also Londi Erazo's Let's play, running on loop on the Wax Heads store page. So please do check them out if you haven't seen them already.

notes.title: Wax Heads: Now available on Mac!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44982268/64930f860722fb7663028f354687f0b60c5adfa8.png[/img]

Hello fellow Wax Heads!

We hope you're all enjoying the summer :)

We have exciting news: [b]Wax Heads' demo is now available to play on Steam for all Mac users!!
[/b]
It's something we've had a lot of requests for, so we're very happy we could open up the opportunity for more people to check out Repeater Records and recommend some excellent albums ^ ^ . 

Otherwise in other news we recently announced that Wax Heads will be taking part in Indie Dev Day in Barcelona in September and SXSW Sydney in October, both of which we're very excited about.

But also, just to say again, we're still blown away with the positive response we've been getting to the announcement of Wax Heads, and as a way of saying thank you - we wanted to share a sneak peek of what we've been working on.

Firstly - here is a first look of the core crew of employees you'll be working alongside in Wax Heads; Morgan and Hank you'll know from the demo, Tee you might recognise from our Key Art, but we're happy to introduce Matteo, Paul and Abi as the other half of the pack. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44982268/7575d54f5eb071cc8bf2fc1f8db08b40fb69d61a.png[/img]
(We can't wait to tell you more about them and their knotty, entangled lives that will spill out all over the course of the full game!) 

Secondly, one important feature we think for Wax Heads is, the immersion of getting to enjoy working in a record store. As such, we've been experimenting with ways to create more of playful interactions, such as thinking how to start each and every new exciting day at Repeater Records. Take a look:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44982268/00c9ae469aaac328cd92e91ab0cc776355cff1f0.gif[/img]

Thirdly, (and this is more just for fun), Murray recreated one of his favourite albums in Wax Heads form. He's so endeared by it he's considering turning it into a tshirt!  Let us know if you think that's a good idea below in the comments!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44982268/3b637389dc997fed34bdc2c65bf7c0ecb3347325.png[/img]
This is just the tip of the iceberg of what we're up to, but we're super happy to share even this little bit of it with you all on our journey. Thank you for your support, it means everything. 

Stay tuned for future updates, but until then take care and keep on spinning! 

Patattie Games <3

And there's more fun things to come, but for now we're just so happy with the response since we've gotten since we announced, thank you all for checking us out, wishlisting, playing and sharing - we're so excited to share more about the world of Wax Heads with you!!!

For now keep on spinning and keep your eyes peeled for that update with the new customer dropping tomorrow! 

<3
